problems.text: binomial chance: n 8, p 1/2, exactly 6; coin
problems.explain: Any one order of 6 heads and 2 tails has probability (1/2)⁶(1/2)², and there are C(8, 6) = 28 orders: C(8, 6)(1/2)⁶(1/2)² = 28 × 1/256 = 28/256. So the probability is 7/64.

prompt.v: A fair coin is tossed 8 times. What is the probability of exactly 7 heads?

problems.text: binomial chance: n 8, p 1/2, exactly 7; coin
problems.explain: Any one order of 7 heads and 1 tail has probability (1/2)⁷(1/2)¹, and there are C(8, 7) = 8 orders: C(8, 7)(1/2)⁷(1/2)¹ = 8 × 1/256 = 8/256. So the probability is 1/32.
